interactions_checked.interaction: Tacrolimus inhibits CYP3A4, increasing atorvastatin plasma levels and risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis
interactions_checked.action: Monitor CK and liver enzymes; consider switching atorvastatin to pravastatin 40 mg or rosuvastatin 10 mg

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined effect on renal haemodynamics may raise serum creatinine and potassium
interactions_checked.action: Check serum creatinine and potassium 1–2 weeks after any dose change; adjust lisinopril if needed

interactions_checked.interaction: Beta‑blocker masks adrenergic symptoms of hypoglycaemia, increasing risk of severe hypoglycaemia
interactions_checked.action: Discontinue insulin (as above) and monitor glucose closely if any insulin is re‑introduced

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive risk of electrolyte disturbance and renal function decline in severe CKD
Combined antiplatelet effect increases bleeding risk
interactions_checked.action: Monitor full blood count and signs of bleeding; standard DAPT monitoring

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can increase statin concentrations via CYP3A4 inhibition
interactions_checked.action: Monitor for statin‑related adverse effects; consider dose reduction or alternative statin if symptoms arise

contraindications.reason: High‑dose thiazide contraindicated in severe CKD (eGFR 6.1 mL/min) and worsens glucose tolerance per NICE
contraindications.alternative: Discontinue; use amlodipine 5 mg as antihypertensive

contraindications.reason: NICE lists beta‑blockers as contraindicated for first‑line hypertension because they may worsen glucose tolerance and mask hypoglycaemia; however it is justified for post‑ACS management
contraindications.alternative: Continue only for ACS indication; do not rely on it as sole antihypertensive

treatment_summary: Continue guideline‑recommended cardiovascular drugs (atorvastatin, lisinopril, aspirin, prasugrel, atenolol) for secondary prevention of NSTEMI and hypertension, while monitoring renal function and drug levels. Discontinue high‑dose hydrochlorothiazide due to severe CKD and replace with amlodipine 5 mg. Stop insulin because the patient is normoglycaemic (HbA1c 4.1%) and at high hypoglycaemia risk with beta‑blockade. Monitor for interactions (statin‑tacrolimus, ACE‑I‑tacrolimus, statin‑amlodipine) and adjust therapy as needed. Provide non‑pharmacological advice on diet, exercise, smoking cessation, and refer to diabetes prevention and cardiac rehabilitation programmes.
